title: LKAS 12 - Income Taxes
description: A highly challenging assessment of current tax, deferred tax, tax bases, temporary differences, recognition, measurement, revaluations and the application of LKAS 12 to complex accounting scenarios.
subject: ACC2373 - Advanced Financial Accounting and Reporting

questions.question: Which statement best explains the principal accounting issue addressed by LKAS 12?
options: Determining only the amount of income tax currently payable to taxation authorities
Accounting for current and future tax consequences arising from recognised assets, liabilities, transactions and other events
Reconciling every difference between accounting profit and taxable profit through deferred tax recognition
Ensuring that accounting profit and taxable profit become equal over the life of an entity
questions.answer: Accounting for current and future tax consequences arising from recognised assets, liabilities, transactions and other events
questions.rationale: LKAS 12 addresses both current tax consequences and future tax consequences arising from recovery or settlement of recognised assets and liabilities and from transactions and events recognised in the financial statements.

questions.question: An entity reports accounting profit of Rs. 5 million and faces a corporate tax rate of 30 percent. Why might total tax expense differ from Rs. 1.5 million?
options: Because tax expense includes only deferred tax and excludes current tax
Because accounting profit is calculated after deducting current tax but before deferred tax
Because tax expense may reflect both current tax based on taxable profit and deferred tax arising from temporary differences
Because every difference between accounting profit and taxable profit permanently changes the deferred tax balance
questions.answer: Because tax expense may reflect both current tax based on taxable profit and deferred tax arising from temporary differences
questions.rationale: Tax expense comprises current tax and deferred tax. Taxable profit can differ from accounting profit, while temporary differences may create deferred tax expense or income.

questions.question: A machine originally cost Rs. 1,000,000. Tax depreciation of Rs. 400,000 has been claimed and the remaining amount will be deductible against taxable economic benefits generated by recovery of the machine. What is its tax base?
options: Nil
questions.rationale: The tax base of an asset is the amount that will be deductible against taxable economic benefits when its carrying amount is recovered. The remaining tax deduction is Rs. 600,000.

questions.question: Interest receivable has a carrying amount of Rs. 300,000. The interest has been recognised as accounting income but will be taxed only when cash is collected. What is the tax base of the receivable?
options: Rs. 300,000 because the receivable represents a recognised asset
Nil because no amount will be deductible against the taxable economic benefits arising on collection
Rs. 90,000 because the tax base equals the expected tax payable
Rs. 210,000 because the carrying amount must be stated net of future tax
questions.answer: Nil because no amount will be deductible against the taxable economic benefits arising on collection
questions.rationale: The future collection will be taxable and no tax deduction is available against that taxable amount. Therefore, the tax base of the interest receivable is nil.

questions.question: Trade receivables have a carrying amount of Rs. 800,000 and the related sales revenue has already been included in taxable profit. Assuming collection of the receivables has no further tax consequences, what is their tax base?
options: Nil because receivables do not generate tax deductions
Rs. 240,000 because this represents the tax already attributable to the revenue
Rs. 560,000 because future collection is effectively net of tax
Rs. 800,000 because recovery of the carrying amount will have no further tax consequences
questions.answer: Rs. 800,000 because recovery of the carrying amount will have no further tax consequences
questions.rationale: When the related revenue has already been taxed, collecting the receivable creates no additional taxable amount. The tax base therefore equals the carrying amount.

questions.question: An accrued expense liability has a carrying amount of Rs. 500,000. The expense becomes deductible for tax purposes only when it is paid. What is the tax base of the liability?
options: Rs. 500,000 because the liability is recognised in full
Rs. 350,000 because the future deduction should be adjusted for tax
Nil because the entire carrying amount will be deductible in a future period
Rs. 150,000 because this represents the future tax saving
questions.answer: Nil because the entire carrying amount will be deductible in a future period
questions.rationale: The tax base of a liability equals its carrying amount less amounts deductible in future periods. Therefore, Rs. 500,000 less Rs. 500,000 gives a tax base of nil.

questions.question: A company has accrued fines of Rs. 200,000. The fines are permanently non-deductible for taxation purposes. Which combination is correct?
options: Tax base nil and a deductible temporary difference of Rs. 200,000
Tax base Rs. 200,000 and no temporary difference
Tax base nil and a taxable temporary difference of Rs. 200,000
Tax base Rs. 140,000 and a deductible temporary difference of Rs. 60,000
questions.answer: Tax base Rs. 200,000 and no temporary difference
questions.rationale: No future tax deduction will arise when the fine is settled. Therefore, the tax base equals the carrying amount and no temporary difference exists.

questions.question: A loan payable has a carrying amount of Rs. 4 million and repayment of the principal will have no tax consequences. What is the most appropriate deferred tax conclusion?
options: The tax base is nil and a deferred tax asset arises
The tax base is Rs. 4 million and no temporary difference arises
The tax base is nil and a deferred tax liability arises
The tax base depends entirely on the corporate income tax rate
questions.answer: The tax base is Rs. 4 million and no temporary difference arises
questions.rationale: Because repayment has no tax consequences, the liability's tax base equals its carrying amount and there is no temporary difference.

questions.question: An asset has a carrying amount of Rs. 900,000 and a tax base of Rs. 650,000. Assuming no recognition exception applies, which conclusion is correct?
options: A deductible temporary difference of Rs. 250,000 creates a deferred tax asset
A taxable temporary difference of Rs. 250,000 creates a deferred tax liability
A taxable temporary difference of Rs. 650,000 creates a deferred tax liability
No temporary difference exists until the asset is actually recovered
questions.answer: A taxable temporary difference of Rs. 250,000 creates a deferred tax liability
questions.rationale: For an asset, a carrying amount exceeding its tax base normally means future taxable economic benefits will exceed available future tax deductions, creating a taxable temporary difference.

questions.question: A liability has a carrying amount of Rs. 400,000 and a tax base of Rs. 100,000 because Rs. 300,000 will become deductible when the liability is settled. Assuming recognition criteria are satisfied, what arises?
options: A deferred tax liability based on Rs. 300,000
A deferred tax asset based on Rs. 300,000
A deferred tax asset based on Rs. 100,000
No deferred tax because the deduction has not yet been claimed
questions.answer: A deferred tax asset based on Rs. 300,000
questions.rationale: The settlement of the liability will generate a future tax deduction of Rs. 300,000. This deductible temporary difference gives rise to a deferred tax asset subject to the probability criterion.

questions.question: A machine costing Rs. 1 million is depreciated at 25 percent per year for accounting purposes and 30 percent per year for tax purposes. At the end of the first year, with a tax rate of 30 percent, what deferred tax balance arises?
options: A deferred tax asset of Rs. 15,000
A deferred tax liability of Rs. 90,000
A deferred tax liability of Rs. 15,000
A deferred tax asset of Rs. 75,000
questions.answer: A deferred tax liability of Rs. 15,000
questions.rationale: The carrying amount is Rs. 750,000 and the tax base is Rs. 700,000. The taxable temporary difference is Rs. 50,000, producing a deferred tax liability of Rs. 15,000.

questions.question: A company claims tax depreciation faster than accounting depreciation during the early years of an asset's life. Assuming the total depreciable amount is eventually the same for accounting and tax purposes, what is the most likely pattern?
options: Current tax is initially reduced while a deferred tax liability arises and later reverses
Current tax is initially increased while a deferred tax asset arises and never reverses
Total tax expense is permanently reduced by the accelerated tax depreciation
No deferred tax arises because depreciation differences always represent permanent differences
questions.answer: Current tax is initially reduced while a deferred tax liability arises and later reverses
questions.rationale: Accelerated tax depreciation creates larger early tax deductions and lower current tax, but also normally creates a taxable temporary difference that reverses in later periods.

questions.question: A property has a carrying amount of Rs. 8 million and a tax base of Rs. 6 million immediately before revaluation. It is then revalued to Rs. 10 million without any adjustment to its tax base. At a tax rate of 30 percent, what is the total deferred tax liability immediately after revaluation?
questions.rationale: After revaluation, the carrying amount is Rs. 10 million and the tax base remains Rs. 6 million. The taxable temporary difference is Rs. 4 million, giving a deferred tax liability of Rs. 1.2 million.

questions.question: Using the property in the previous scenario, what amount of additional deferred tax arises specifically because of the Rs. 2 million revaluation increase?
questions.rationale: The revaluation itself increases the taxable temporary difference by Rs. 2 million. At 30 percent, the additional deferred tax liability is Rs. 600,000.

questions.question: A revaluation gain is recognised in other comprehensive income and creates an additional deferred tax liability. Where should the corresponding deferred tax effect generally be recognised?
options: Entirely in current tax payable because deferred tax cannot arise from revaluations
In other comprehensive income because the tax effect follows the underlying transaction
In profit or loss because all deferred tax movements are tax expenses
Directly against the carrying amount of the revalued asset
questions.answer: In other comprehensive income because the tax effect follows the underlying transaction
questions.rationale: LKAS 12 generally requires the tax consequences of a transaction to be recognised consistently with the underlying transaction. Tax related to an item recognised in other comprehensive income is therefore also recognised there.

questions.question: An entity purchases equipment for Rs. 2 million. No tax deductions are available for depreciation or disposal losses, and disposal gains are not taxable. The transaction is not a business combination, affects neither accounting nor taxable profit on initial recognition and does not create equal taxable and deductible temporary differences. What is the appropriate treatment on initial recognition?
options: Recognise a deferred tax liability of Rs. 600,000 immediately
Recognise a deferred tax asset because future depreciation is non-deductible
Do not recognise the resulting deferred tax because the initial recognition exemption applies
Recognise deferred tax only after the first accounting depreciation charge
questions.answer: Do not recognise the resulting deferred tax because the initial recognition exemption applies
questions.rationale: The initial recognition exemption applies when the qualifying transaction is not a business combination, affects neither accounting nor taxable profit and does not create equal taxable and deductible temporary differences.

questions.question: Which statement most accurately describes recognition of a deferred tax asset arising from a deductible temporary difference?
options: It must be recognised for every deductible temporary difference regardless of future profitability
It is recognised only after the related tax deduction has actually been claimed
It is recognised to the extent that it is probable that taxable profit will be available against which the difference can be utilised
It is recognised only when an equivalent deferred tax liability exists in the same reporting period
questions.answer: It is recognised to the extent that it is probable that taxable profit will be available against which the difference can be utilised
questions.rationale: The recognition of a deferred tax asset depends on the probability that sufficient taxable profit will be available to utilise the future tax deduction.

questions.question: A company recognises a warranty provision of Rs. 2 million. Warranty costs become deductible only when claims are paid. The tax rate is 30 percent and sufficient future taxable profit is probable. What is the deferred tax effect?
options: A deferred tax liability of Rs. 600,000
A deferred tax asset of Rs. 600,000
A deferred tax asset of Rs. 1.4 million
No deferred tax because the provision is only an accounting estimate
questions.answer: A deferred tax asset of Rs. 600,000
questions.rationale: The liability has a carrying amount of Rs. 2 million and a tax base of nil, creating a deductible temporary difference of Rs. 2 million and a deferred tax asset of Rs. 600,000.

questions.question: A company records an allowance for doubtful debts of Rs. 80,000. Tax law permits a deduction only when specific debts are actually written off. Assuming future taxable profit is probable, what is the most likely deferred tax consequence at a 30 percent tax rate?
options: A deferred tax asset of Rs. 24,000
A deferred tax liability of Rs. 24,000
A deferred tax asset of Rs. 56,000
No deferred tax because doubtful debts affect both accounting and taxation eventually
questions.answer: A deferred tax asset of Rs. 24,000
questions.rationale: The accounting allowance reduces the carrying amount before the tax deduction becomes available, creating a deductible temporary difference and a deferred tax asset.

questions.question: A company incurs development expenditure of Rs. 160,000 during the year and capitalises the full amount for accounting purposes. Tax legislation permits an immediate deduction equal to 125 percent of the expenditure. Ignoring any accounting amortisation, what is the immediate effect on taxable profit compared with accounting profit?
options: Taxable profit is Rs. 160,000 lower because only the actual expenditure is deductible
Taxable profit is Rs. 200,000 lower because the enhanced deduction is available while no accounting expense is recognised
Taxable profit is Rs. 40,000 lower because only the additional 25 percent creates a difference
Taxable profit is Rs. 200,000 higher because capitalised development costs cannot affect taxation
questions.answer: Taxable profit is Rs. 200,000 lower because the enhanced deduction is available while no accounting expense is recognised
questions.rationale: The tax deduction is 125 percent of Rs. 160,000, which equals Rs. 200,000. Because the expenditure is capitalised rather than expensed for accounting purposes, the full deduction reduces taxable profit relative to accounting profit in the current period.

questions.question: A development asset has a carrying amount of Rs. 230,000. The related expenditure has already been fully deducted for tax purposes and no further tax deductions are available from recovering the asset. Which deferred tax consequence normally follows at a 30 percent rate?
options: A deferred tax asset of Rs. 69,000
A deferred tax liability of Rs. 69,000
A deferred tax liability of Rs. 230,000
No deferred tax because the expenditure has already received tax relief
questions.answer: A deferred tax liability of Rs. 69,000
questions.rationale: The tax base is nil because no future deduction remains. The carrying amount of Rs. 230,000 therefore creates a taxable temporary difference and a deferred tax liability of Rs. 69,000.

questions.question: An entity has unused tax losses of Rs. 5 million. Management forecasts future taxable profit of only Rs. 2 million before the losses expire, and no other convincing evidence supports greater utilisation. At a tax rate of 30 percent, what deferred tax asset is generally supportable?
options: Rs. 1.5 million because the entire tax loss must be recognised
Rs. 600,000 because recognition is limited to losses expected to be utilised
Rs. 900,000 because more than half of the losses remain unused
Nil because a history of tax losses always prohibits deferred tax asset recognition
questions.answer: Rs. 600,000 because recognition is limited to losses expected to be utilised
questions.rationale: A deferred tax asset for unused losses is recognised only to the extent that sufficient future taxable profit is probable. Rs. 2 million multiplied by 30 percent gives Rs. 600,000.

questions.question: An entity with a history of recent tax losses seeks to recognise a large deferred tax asset for unused tax losses. Which evidence would provide the strongest support for recognition?
options: Management believes that every business eventually becomes profitable
The losses have existed for several years and therefore are more likely to reverse automatically
Sufficient taxable temporary differences will reverse before the losses expire or convincing evidence demonstrates adequate future taxable profit
The entity has recognised accounting profits in prior periods even though those periods also produced tax losses
questions.answer: Sufficient taxable temporary differences will reverse before the losses expire or convincing evidence demonstrates adequate future taxable profit
questions.rationale: Recent losses are strong evidence that future taxable profit may not be available, so recognition requires sufficient taxable temporary differences or other convincing evidence of future taxable profit.

questions.question: A deferred tax asset was not recognised in the previous year because future taxable profit was not considered probable. Trading conditions improve significantly during the current year and reliable forecasts now support sufficient taxable profit. What does LKAS 12 require?
options: The asset must remain permanently unrecognised because the original assessment cannot be revised
The entity should recognise the previously unrecognised deferred tax asset to the extent that recovery has become probable
The asset can be recognised only when the underlying temporary difference actually reverses
The entity should recognise the entire possible tax benefit regardless of the revised profitability forecast
questions.answer: The entity should recognise the previously unrecognised deferred tax asset to the extent that recovery has become probable
questions.rationale: Unrecognised deferred tax assets are reassessed at each reporting date and recognised when changed circumstances make future utilisation probable.

questions.question: At the reporting date, the current corporate tax rate is 28 percent. Legislation has been substantively enacted to increase the rate to 32 percent before a taxable temporary difference is expected to reverse. Which rate should normally be used to measure the deferred tax liability?
options: 28 percent because it is the rate applying at the reporting date
30 percent because an average of current and future rates must be used
32 percent because it is expected to apply when the temporary difference reverses
The rate cannot be determined until the temporary difference actually reverses
questions.answer: 32 percent because it is expected to apply when the temporary difference reverses
questions.rationale: Deferred tax is measured using enacted or substantively enacted tax rates expected to apply when the asset is realised or the liability is settled.

questions.question: Why are deferred tax assets and deferred tax liabilities generally not discounted to present value under LKAS 12?
options: Because deferred tax always reverses exactly one year after initial recognition
Because accurately determining the detailed timing of reversals would often be complex or impracticable
Because discounting would always increase rather than decrease deferred tax balances
Because deferred tax represents equity rather than a future tax consequence
questions.answer: Because accurately determining the detailed timing of reversals would often be complex or impracticable
questions.rationale: LKAS 12 prohibits discounting deferred tax balances, with practical difficulties in reliably scheduling the reversal of individual temporary differences being an important underlying reason.

questions.question: An asset has a carrying amount of Rs. 100 and a tax base of Rs. 60. The applicable tax rate is 20 percent if the asset is sold and 30 percent if it is recovered through use. Management expects to sell the asset without further use. What deferred tax liability should be recognised?
options: Rs. 12
Rs. 20
Rs. 8
Rs. 30
questions.answer: Rs. 8
questions.rationale: Measurement reflects the expected manner of recovery. The taxable temporary difference is Rs. 40 and the sale tax rate is 20 percent, producing a deferred tax liability of Rs. 8.

questions.question: An entity recognises a product warranty expense of Rs. 100,000 in accounting profit this year. The amount is deductible for tax purposes only when paid next year. Ignoring other differences, which statement best explains the effect across the two periods?
options: The difference is permanent because the accounting and tax deductions occur in different periods
A deductible temporary difference arises now and reverses when the tax deduction is obtained
A taxable temporary difference arises now because taxable profit is initially higher than accounting profit
No deferred tax arises because the total deduction is identical over the two periods
questions.answer: A deductible temporary difference arises now and reverses when the tax deduction is obtained
questions.rationale: Although current taxable profit is initially higher, the future tax deduction creates a deductible temporary difference and therefore potentially a deferred tax asset.

questions.question: A company has accounting profit before tax of Rs. 105,000 each year. Accounting depreciation is Rs. 25,000 annually, while tax depreciation on a Rs. 100,000 asset is 50 percent annually. All other accounting income and expenses are taxable or deductible in the same period. At a 30 percent tax rate, what is current tax for the first year?
questions.rationale: Accounting profit of Rs. 105,000 includes accounting depreciation of Rs. 25,000. Replacing this with tax depreciation of Rs. 50,000 gives taxable profit of Rs. 80,000 and current tax of Rs. 24,000.

questions.question: Using the same facts, what deferred tax liability exists at the end of the first year?
questions.rationale: The carrying amount after accounting depreciation is Rs. 75,000 and the tax base after tax depreciation is Rs. 50,000. The taxable temporary difference of Rs. 25,000 creates a deferred tax liability of Rs. 7,500.

questions.question: In the second year of the same example, the asset's carrying amount becomes Rs. 50,000 while its tax base becomes nil. What is the closing deferred tax liability at 30 percent?
options: Nil
questions.rationale: The taxable temporary difference is Rs. 50,000 because the carrying amount is Rs. 50,000 and the tax base is nil. At 30 percent, the deferred tax liability is Rs. 15,000.

questions.question: In the third year of the same example, no further tax depreciation is available but accounting depreciation of Rs. 25,000 continues. What is the most accurate description of the deferred tax effect during the year?
options: The deferred tax liability increases because accounting depreciation exceeds tax depreciation
The deferred tax liability decreases as the taxable temporary difference begins to reverse
A new deferred tax asset arises because no tax depreciation is available
The deferred tax balance remains unchanged until the asset is fully depreciated
questions.answer: The deferred tax liability decreases as the taxable temporary difference begins to reverse
questions.rationale: Once tax depreciation has been exhausted, accounting depreciation reduces the carrying amount while the tax base remains nil, causing the previously accumulated taxable temporary difference and deferred tax liability to reverse.

questions.question: Grace Ltd reports accounting profit before tax of Rs. 80,000. Included are accounting depreciation of Rs. 7,000, doubtful debts expense of Rs. 3,000 and long-service leave expense of Rs. 4,000. Tax depreciation is Rs. 8,000, bad debts written off are Rs. 2,000 and no long-service leave is paid. What is taxable profit before considering any other adjustments?
questions.rationale: Starting from Rs. 80,000, add back accounting depreciation of Rs. 7,000, doubtful debts of Rs. 3,000 and long-service leave of Rs. 4,000, then deduct tax depreciation of Rs. 8,000 and bad debts written off of Rs. 2,000. Taxable profit is Rs. 84,000.

questions.question: My Bag Ltd has an opening provision for long-service leave of Rs. 62,000 and a closing provision of Rs. 48,000. Long-service leave expense recognised during the year is Rs. 36,000 and tax deductions are available only when payments are made. How much long-service leave was paid during the year?
questions.rationale: Using the provision movement, opening provision of Rs. 62,000 plus expense of Rs. 36,000 less payments equals the closing provision of Rs. 48,000. Therefore, payments were Rs. 50,000.

questions.question: My Bag Ltd has plant costing Rs. 600,000 with accumulated accounting depreciation of Rs. 190,000 and accumulated tax depreciation of Rs. 280,000 at year end. At a tax rate of 30 percent, which deferred tax position arises from the plant?
options: A deferred tax asset of Rs. 27,000 because accounting depreciation is lower than tax depreciation
A deferred tax liability of Rs. 84,000 because the tax base equals accumulated tax depreciation
A deferred tax liability of Rs. 27,000 because the carrying amount exceeds the tax base by Rs. 90,000
A deferred tax asset of Rs. 90,000 because future accounting depreciation exceeds future tax depreciation
questions.answer: A deferred tax liability of Rs. 27,000 because the carrying amount exceeds the tax base by Rs. 90,000
questions.rationale: The carrying amount is Rs. 410,000 and the tax base is Rs. 320,000. The resulting taxable temporary difference of Rs. 90,000 creates a deferred tax liability of Rs. 27,000 at a 30 percent tax rate.
